items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Dr. Leo B. Mayer on Madison Avenue, who was President Roosevelt's doctor

ctx.x: So you say you hadn't said anything to your wife yet?

I said I hadn't said anything to my wife yet, and I was at Joe Thomas and Laverne Thomas's house at 160th, who lived around the corner, and I had gone there for dinner, and found I had to loosen up, because they kept asking me what's wrong with me. Well, naturally I can't be too lively, knowing that the man said I had to have the operation over again, is what I'm saying to you.

So I knew I had to tell my agent; I had to call him from somewhere, so I opened up and told them. Then I called my agent, and he was the man who suggested (unintelligible) and he said, "Are you sure?" And I said, "I'll tell you what the man said." So we had a consultation -- I spent $85 and went to a Doctor Shine for $35 on Fifth Avenue, and went to Dr. Leo B.
